items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: Horace Henderson was giving us arrangements for Charlie Barnett.

ctx.x: And then I had my freedom musically, and I was with him almost two years before I went with -- we will get into that little by little, but he made some tremendous things with several Barnet bands, record dates I'm talking about like 'Blue Juice' and 'Charleston Alley' and 'Little Smack' was writing for us then, Horace Henderson was giving us arrangements for Charlie Barnett.

items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: He was in that band when I was connected with it

ctx.x: He was in that band when I was connected with it, and of course, that is where I ran into Lena Horne. Charley Barnet was in New York City, and he had a trombone player with him at that time that played trombone with a valve -- a bass trombone where you could hit that low note with that key, you know, and his name was Ford Leary. A big guy. He had four trombone players, and Ford Leary was the guy that Barnet featured singing Shadrack.
